constructs: math.multiplication.factor_referent_mapping (which factor names groups vs. items per group)
prerequisites: Counts by 2s, 5s, and 10s from a stated starting point
Recognizes when a collection is partitioned into equal-sized groups
Reads rows and columns of an array as a structured count
Writes and reads the a x b = c notation form
Extracts two quantities and the question asked from a one-sentence word problem
Single-digit addition used as a checking strategy rather than a substitute operation

included: Factor families x2, x5, x10 only
Equal-groups contexts with stated group count and stated items per group
Rectangular arrays with rows and columns both visible or stated
Skip-counting as a route to a product
Translating an equal-groups or array situation into a x b = c notation
Stating what each factor refers to in the situation
excluded: Formal statement of the commutative property as a named rule
Area or measurement interpretations of multiplication

assumptions.claim: Guided performance materially overstates Reina's unsupported performance on this unit; the 90% guided figure should not be used to set independent expectations.
assumptions.uncertainty: The guided and independent samples covered different sub-constructs (equal groups vs. arrays) and the independent sample was only 5 items, so part of the 90%-to-40% drop may be construct difference rather than support removal.
assumptions.falsifyingEvidence: An unassisted, unseen equal-groups probe of 10+ items scoring at or near the guided level (>=0.85).

assumptions.claim: Reina's most frequent documented error is mis-assigning which quantity is the number of groups and which is the number of items per group, indicating unstable mapping between situation structure and the two factors.
assumptions.uncertainty: In a bare equal-groups product, swapping the two factors does not change the numerical answer, so the marked items must have required structural labeling, a drawing, or a specific referent; the packet does not contain item text or scoring keys, so the mechanism behind these three marked-wrong items is not established.
assumptions.falsifyingEvidence: Item-level extraction showing the three items were marked wrong for a different reason (e.g., miscount, unanswered, copied wrong number) rather than reversed referents.

assumptions.claim: On a minority of items Reina substitutes addition for multiplication rather than reasoning from group structure.
assumptions.uncertainty: Only two items showed this and the observation says the addition was unrelated to the represented groups; whether this reflects operation-selection failure, a misread problem, or abandoning an unfinished strategy is not established.
assumptions.falsifyingEvidence: An unassisted probe in which Reina selects multiplication (or correct repeated addition matching the groups) on all equal-groups items while still making other errors.

assumptions.claim: The prior 60%-80% returned-work band was set too high; the model of Reina's unsupported accuracy on this unit should be shifted downward.
assumptions.uncertainty: Assistance condition on the returned work was not confirmed and the work was completed at school, so the 5/10 could reflect either a lower true level or unmodeled test conditions (time limits, distraction, unfinished items).
assumptions.falsifyingEvidence: Confirmation that the returned work was completed under atypical conditions (e.g., truncated time, missed instruction) plus an unassisted probe in the 60%-80% range.

assumptions.claim: There is no evidence in this packet about Reina's unassisted x2/x5/x10 fact retrieval or skip-counting accuracy, so it must be measured before it is assumed available as a prerequisite.
assumptions.uncertainty: The returned work likely contained fluency items but no per-item breakdown by item type is available, so fluency accuracy is genuinely unknown rather than low.
assumptions.falsifyingEvidence: Returned-work item extraction or a fluency probe establishing x2/x5/x10 retrieval accuracy.

assumptions.claim: The recorded likes and completions are engagement-stream records from spelling activities and establish nothing about Reina's multiplication knowledge, preferences, or ability.
assumptions.uncertainty: Engagement records are low-confidence (0.45) and drawn from a different subject; likes with only two of four completions do not indicate sustained engagement either.
assumptions.falsifyingEvidence: Academic-stream evidence from mathematics activities carrying its own accuracy record.

predictedErrorPatterns: assigns the group count to items-per-group and vice versa
gives a correct product but cannot say which factor is which
on array items, reports total or one dimension when asked for the other
academicPredictions.maximumClaim: unassisted baseline level only; no mastery or instructional-effect claim

academicPredictions.expectedOutcome: On an unassisted, untimed probe of 12 unseen x2/x5/x10 fact items, accuracy is measurable but the band is wide because no fluency evidence exists in the packet; x10 items are answered more accurately than x2 items.
predictedErrorPatterns: off-by-one-group skip-counting errors (e.g., 5x5 answered as 20 or 30)
loses count on the longer x2 chains
answers x10 by appending a zero while x2 and x5 require counting
academicPredictions.maximumClaim: descriptive baseline only; wide band reflects absent evidence

academicPredictions.expectedOutcome: After explicit referent-labeling instruction and faded guided practice, an unassisted delayed probe (5-10 days later) of 10 unseen equal-groups and array items scores above the 40% independent array figure but below the 90% guided figure, with residual errors concentrated on array items rather than equal-groups items.
predictedErrorPatterns: residual reversal of rows and items-per-row on arrays
correct product with an unlabeled or mislabeled representation
occasional additive substitution on the last items of the probe
academicPredictions.maximumClaim: retained independent performance on unseen items; not classroom-level mastery

academicPredictions.expectedOutcome: The next returned graded assignment covering this unit scores in a downward-recalibrated band relative to the prior 60%-80% prediction, and additive-substitution errors do not exceed two items.

addition used in place of multiplication on at most two items

planningRationale: The prior cycle's single preregistered prediction failed: returned work came in at 5/10, below the 60%-80% band, so the planner's model of Reina's unsupported level was too optimistic and the guided 90% figure was weighted too heavily against the unassisted 40% figure. The returned error pattern partly confirmed the predicted groups/items reversal but also produced an unpredicted class of error - two items using addition unrelated to the represented groups - which the prior program did not anticipate. Two consequences follow. First, all expectation bands are shifted downward and widened, and guided results are quarantined from independent results at every node. Second, the plan treats the reversal claim as provisional rather than settled, because reversing the two factors in a bare equal-groups product does not change the numeric answer, so the marked items must have demanded structural labeling that the packet does not document; item-level text is therefore requested rather than assumed. The sequence is deliberately short: one unassisted baseline that separates fact retrieval, referent mapping, and operation selection (none of which the packet currently distinguishes), one narrow teaching node on referent labeling, one guided node with tiered fading so the support-removal gap is measured rather than inferred, and two unassisted probes, one immediate and one delayed, to supply the retention datum that returned work alone cannot supply. Nothing about Reina's interests, dispositions, or general ability is inferred; the engagement records come from spelling activities, carry 0.45 confidence, and show two completions out of four initiations, so they are excluded from academic reasoning entirely. The next educational question is: when the number of groups and the number of items per group must be named rather than merely multiplied, can Reina assign each quantity to the correct role without support, and does that assignment survive a five-to-ten-day delay?
